fields.title: Phosphoproteomics of consecuively active AKT in liver and Insulin stimulated primary Hepatocytes
fields.description: Liver mitochondria play a central role in metabolic adaptations to changing nutritional states, yet their dynamic regulation upon anticipated changes in the energy state has remained unaddressed. Here, we show that sensory food perception rapidly induces mitochondrial fission in the liver via protein kinase B/AKT-dependent phosphorylation of serine 131 of the Mitochondrial fission factor (MFFS131), a response mediated via activation of hypothalamic Pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC)-expressing neurons. A non-phosphorylatable MFFS131G knock-in mutation abrogates AKT-induced mitochondrial fragmentation in vitro. In vivo, MFFS131G knock-in mice display altered liver mitochondrial dynamics upon refeeding and impaired insulin stimulated suppression of gluconeogenesis. Collectively, we reveal a critical role for rapid activation of a hypothalamic/liver axis to adapt mitochondrial function to anticipated changes of nutritional state in control of hepatic glucose metabolism.  R26-fl-Akt-C mice   Mice carrying a conditional myristoylation tagged Akt-C transgene in the ROSA26 locus were used to activate AKT in the liver with a liver specific Cre-dependent virus. The generation of this line has been described previously (V. Kohlhaas et al, 2021)  For AAV mediated liver-specific delivery of Cre, R26-fl-Akt-C or control mice were injected with a AAV8-TBG-iCre virus (VB1724, Vector Biolabs).  This repository contains two experiments a) Liver of liver active Akt-CA and b) Insulin stimulation of primary heptocytes. Please note that replicate one of the hepatocyte dataset have been removed from the analysis due to the limited number of posphosites compared to others.
fields.sample_protocol: Primary Hepatocytes Isolation To isolate primary hepatocytes, mice were sacrificed by cervical dislocation and the abdomen was opened. A 26G cannula was inserted into the vena cava, the hepatic portal vein was cut and liver was perfused for 5 min with pre-warmed EBSS solution without Mg2+ and Ca2 and with 0.5 M EGTA to remove residual blood from the liver. Afterwards, livers were perfused for 5 min with 50 mL pre-warmed EBSS containing 10 mM HEPES, EBSS with Mg2+ and Ca2, 15 mg collagenase IV and 2 mg trypsin inhibitor (T9128, Sigma). Perfused livers were extracted, the gall bladder was removed and livers were transferred into 10 mL ice cold EBSS with Mg2+, Ca2 and 10 mM HEPES. Isolated cells were filtered through a 100 μm cell strainer, collected in 50 mL falcon and pelleted by centrifugation (270 g, 5 min at 4°C). Cells were washed two times with 10 mL cold hepatocyte cultivation medium (DMEM High Glucose GlutaMAX 61965-059, GIBCO containing 1% sodium pyruvate, 1% non-essential amino acids, 5% fetal calf serum, 1% pen/streo). For mass spectrometry based phosphoproteomics, 3.6x10^6 cells per 10 cm plate seeded (2 Isolations, 5 animals pooled), for final sample submission two plates were pooled - 1 coming from each isolation to avoid batch effects- resulting in 2 10 cm plates per sample pellet). Medium was changed 4 hours after isolation and Cells harvested on the following day. Before snap freezing, Cells were fasted for 3 h in 0.5%FCS medium. 20 min Insulin Stimulation (Sigma I9278). Cell pellet was washed with PBS and collected.   Phosphoproteomics Liver were generated using a liver lysis buffer (Tris 50 mM, NaCl 130 mM, EDTA 5 mM, PMSF 100mM, NaF 100mM). A cOmplete Mini Protease Inhibitor Cocktail (1 tablet/10 mL, 1183617001, Roche) and 1% NP-40 were freshly added. For primary hepatocytes, 7,2 x 106 were washed with PBS, pelleted through rapid centrifugation and snap frozen. Cell pellets were lysed in 4% SDS in 10mM HEPES (pH=8.5) and subjected to sonication (pulse 1s on/off for 1 min, Bandelin Mini20). Protein concentration was measured as described before and 500 µg was subjected to acetone precipitation. 300 μL HEPES (100 mM pH=8.5) was added to the pellet, and proteins were reduced using 10 mM TCEP for 15 min at 37°C and alkylated by 20 mM CAA for 45 min at 45°C. LysC (129-02541, Wako) in 100 mM HEPES pH = 8.5 was added on the pellet in a 1:100 enzyme:substrate ratio and incubated for 2 hours at 37°C with 500 rpm. Trypsin (T6567, Sigma Aldrich) was then added and incubated overnight at 37°C on a ThermoMixer (shaking: 500 rpm). Generated peptides were desalted using the SepPak (Waters, 186000308, 50 mg sorbent). Peptides were eluted using 80% acetonitrile and 0.1% formic acid. Samples were dried to complete dryness in a SpeedVac (Eppendorf Concentrator Plus). A fraction corresponding to 50 µg peptides was collected to measure the whole proteome.  Phosphorylated peptides were enriched using the HighSelect TiO2 Phosphopeptide enrichment kit (A32993, Thermo Fisher Scientific) following the manufacture’s protocol, using peptide equivalent to a total of 500-750 µg protein input (protein input within an experiment was equal). The eluate containing enriched p-sites was dried in a SpeedVac and resuspended in 8 µL 2% formic acid and 2.5% acetonitrile. Liquid Chromatography and Mass Spectrometry for phosphoproteomics  The instrumentation consisted of a nano-LC 1200 (Thermo Fisher Scientific) coupled to a QExploris 480 (Thermo Fisher Scientific) quadrupole-based orbitrap mass spectrometer via a nano-electrospray ionization source. 2 µL of the eluted peptides (SepPak for whole proteome, HighSelect TiO2 tips for phosphopeptides) for were separated using an Aurora 50cm 1.7 µm column (IonOpticks) applying a flow rate of 185 nL/min and a column temperature of 50°C. Peptides were separated on a 120 min gradient using two buffers a) 0.1% formic acid (A) and b) 0.1% formic acid in 80% acetonitrile. The content of buffer B was raised from 4% to 25 % within 100 min followed by an increase to 60%B within 16 min and a 4 min wash step at 60% B. Full MS spectra were acquired using a resolution of 120,000 at 200 m/z and an AGC target of 500% (max inj. T: 20ms, 350-1150Th). The mass spectrometer operated in a data-dependent mode targeting the top-12 peaks for MS/MS fragmentation utilizing an isolation window of 1.2 Th and an MS2 resolution of 30,000 (at 200m/z).  For peptide fragmentation multiple normalized HCD energies were applied (24,0, 28.0, 32.0). The maximum injection time was set to 55 ms. For the whole proteome, a top-22 method combined with an MS2 resolution of 15,000 was selected.  The AGC target was set to 6E5 and spectra were recorded in centroid mode. Dynamic peak exclusion was enabled for 12 s using a mass accuracy of 8 p.p.m. Ions of charge between 2 and 4 were considered for MS/MS. The ion transfer capillary temperature was set to 275°C and 2.4kV was applied as a spray voltage in positive mode.
